ai.title: Everything announced at Amazon’s October 2026 hardware launch
ai.description:
Amazon had plenty of new gadgets to share at its Echo hardware event this year, along with updates to the AI-powered Alexa Plus after it became available to everyone in the US in February. But the big news this year is screens: devices with big, beautiful ones, and those that lack them entirely.
There’s the Alexa Photo Frame, which Amazon devices chief Panos Panay describes as “the world’s smartest photo frame” and that doubles as a full Alexa speaker. There’s also the new Echo Time smart alarm clock, the screenless Echo Studio with Home Camera, a fully redesigned Echo Dot, and Amazon’s latest flagship smart display, the Echo Show 16, which comes with a whopping eight woofers and can run the full Fire TV experience by touch.
You can catch up on all our coverage below, including the six biggest announcements and our hands-on with the Echo Show 16 and Echo Time.

ai.title: Apple to Open Pre-Orders for Five New Products Today
ai.description:
Apple is set to open pre-orders for five new products on Wednesday, including its first yet-to-be-announced touchscreen MacBook Pro models.


Pre-orders will open for the following new products:

iPad mini with OLED display and A20 Pro chip

iMac with M6 chip

14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip

14-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen

16-inch MacBook Pro with OLED touchscreen

Pre-orders for the iPad mini, iMac, and M6 MacBook Pro open at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time, with availability beginning Friday, November 6. The iPad mini starts at $699, the iMac at $1,499, and the M6 MacBook Pro at $1,999. 

Bloomberg reports that pre-orders for the touchscreen MacBook Pro models will also begin Wednesday following their announcement at Apple's "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles, with availability potentially as early as November 6. Pricing is expected to start at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and at least $3,399 for the 16-inch.

ai.title: Apple Shares tvOS 27.2 Release Notes With List of New Features
ai.description:
tvOS 27.2 was released on Monday for the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer, but the Apple TV does not show release notes for software updates in the Settings app. Instead, Apple periodically updates a support document outlining what is new in tvOS updates, and the release notes for tvOS 27.2 are now available.


Note that Apple never released a tvOS 27.1 version, so tvOS 27.2 is the first Apple TV software update since tvOS 27 was released in September.

Find My app now supports the Siri Remote (2nd generation) and later, but Precision Finding is limited to the Siri Remote (4th generation). The update also contains bug fixes and security patches.

This update brings new ways to stay connected with FaceTime, personalize your screen saver, and locate your Siri Remote with Find My, along with bug fixes and security updates for your Apple TV 4K.

FaceTime

FaceTime links make it easier to join calls directly from your Apple TV.

Sign language interpreter and captioning support lets you add third-party services to your calls.

Screen Savers

Photo personalization lets you use your iPhone to choose specific photos for your screen saver without sharing your full library with Apple TV.

Shuffle option lets you enjoy different screen saver categories as your Apple TV cycles through them.

Find My

Apple said Siri AI will be available on the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer, but this functionality is not yet enabled on these models on tvOS 27.2. The new Apple TV 4K (4th generation) launches on Friday, November 13, and Siri AI is one of its headline new features, so perhaps the feature will come to older models closer to then.
